provenance.note: Owner-authorized chapter 3 production authoring, 4 October 2026. Canonical IDs, source activity partitions, exercise-number gaps, known response counts, support timing, targets and purpose paraphrases retain local S18/unified evidence. Japanese sentences, readings, translations, banks, mappings, grammar notes, static kanji shape teaching and contextual examples are reviewed authored/adapted content, not source quotations. The five-turn dessert-shop scene has visible Japanese, complete readings/TTS and no English transcript. Its selected-flavor fact is bound to guest-1 and reused by the exact-version delayed checkpoint question. CP context is reviewed separately before launch and has no question transcript or player. L02 one end retry is an explicit app policy for its failed listening occurrence only; base counts and first-attempt accuracy remain separate from retry mastery. L05 optional completion metadata projects its retained tail community endpoint; the original eight rows and raw null metadata remain unchanged. Four-response polite trial suffix reconstruction uses authored でみます after supplied 飲ん, retaining its count without inserting punctuation as a response.

policies.assessment: Equal weight per graded required screen. Teaching is ungraded; core completion, raw first-attempt accuracy and checkpoint pass reporting remain separate. Optional private writing never blocks completion.
policies.incorrectResponses: Final responses and typed Check lock feedback. Wrong pairs permit another match while retaining the screen mistake. The configured L02 listening miss receives one retry after its nine base screens; retry mastery does not replace first-attempt accuracy.
policies.audio: Existing Japanese TTS supplies complete scripts/readings. Required playback gates and all-turn ordered dialogue playback remain; unsupported listening hides Japanese/English until feedback.
policies.visuals: Replaceable neutral media slots defer original photos/video/kanji animations. Static glyph shapes, readings, meanings and examples provide complete teaching without invented stroke order.

unresolvedSourceFacts: Source-identical literal wording, exhaustive accepted variants, randomization and acoustic quality remain unknown; reviewed authoring supplies ordinary literal gaps.
Source rewards, universal retry policies, score threshold boundary and causal unlock enforcement remain unproven; research outcomes never seed app progress.
Recorded recap/replay controls do not establish unobserved recap contents; app correction/audio remains available through shared support.

before.text: 努力をつづけることが大切です。
before.secondary: どりょくをつづけることがたいせつです。

before.text: It is important to keep making an effort.
努力（どりょく）is a noun. 努力する means make an effort. つづけること nominalizes continuing.

audio.text: 努力をつづけることが大切です。
audio.reading: どりょくをつづけることがたいせつです。

sourceContract.purpose: Effort noun with continuation and nominalisation context

before.secondary: らいねん、にほんごのしけんをうけようとおもっています。

before.text: I intend to take a Japanese exam next year.
試験を受ける is take an exam. 受けようと思っています is a supplied volitional intention; the collocation is the new target.

audio.reading: らいねん、にほんごのしけんをうけようとおもっています。

sourceContract.purpose: Exam-taking collocation in supplied volitional intention

screens.prompt: Choose the natural exam-taking verb in this intention.

after.text: 来年、日本語の試験を受けようと思っています。
after.secondary: らいねん、にほんごのしけんをうけようとおもっています。

after.text: I intend to take a Japanese exam next year.
試験を受ける means take an exam. 受ける is an ichidan verb: 受けよう. 取る is a literal transfer from English “take”, not this collocation; 受かる means pass and takes に with 試験.

audio.text: 来年、日本語の試験を受けようと思っています。
audio.reading: らいねん、にほんごのしけんをうけようとおもっています。
audio.feedbackText: 来年、日本語の試験を受けようと思っています。

sourceContract.purpose: Collocation verb choice against literal-transfer distractor

after.text: 日本語のしけんを受けたいです。
after.secondary: にほんごのしけんをうけたいです。

after.text: I want to take a Japanese exam.
試験 is しけん. テスト can also mean test; use the taught word here.

audio.text: 日本語のしけんを受けたいです。
audio.reading: にほんごのしけんをうけたいです。
audio.feedbackText: 日本語のしけんを受けたいです。

after.text: I want to pass the Japanese exam, so I make an effort every day.
試験に合格する means pass an exam. 努力しています describes ongoing effort.

audio.text: 日本語の試験に合格したいので、毎日努力しています。

screens.prompt: Match each sentence to its grammatical function.

left.text: 明日、浴衣を着てみます。

right.text: Future trial: trying a yukata tomorrow
Ongoing state: wearing a yukata now

after.text: ている describes the ongoing state here; てみる describes a trial action. The 今 and 明日 contexts fix the time.

sourceContract.purpose: Ongoing versus future trial sentence-function contrast

screens.prompt: この料理は初めてです。味を知りたいです。どうしますか。

options.text: 食べたことがありません。

after.text: 味を知りたいので、少し食べてみます。
after.secondary: あじをしりたいので、すこしたべてみます。

after.text: I want to know its flavor, so I will try eating a little.
A small trial answers the desire to find out the flavor. Stating no experience or asking someone not to eat does not propose that trial.

screens.prompt: Listen and read about a lightweight robe.

before.text: 浴衣は、軽い着物の一種です。旅館や夏祭りなどで着ることがあります。夏祭りで浴衣を着てみます。
before.secondary: ゆかたは、かるいきもののいっしゅです。りょかんやなつまつりなどできることがあります。なつまつりでゆかたをきてみます。

before.text: A yukata is a type of lightweight kimono. People may wear one at inns or summer festivals. I will try wearing one at a summer festival.
Yukata use varies by place and occasion. 着てみます describes trying to wear one in this example.

screens.prompt: 浴衣を着てみたいですか。Choose an affirmative desire to try.

options.text: いいえ、着てみたくないです。

after.text: はい、着てみたいです。
Yes, I would like to try wearing one.
みたいです expresses desire; みたくないです is its negative. 着ています describes current wearing, not the requested desire.

sourceContract.purpose: Appropriate trial-desire question response; feedback teaches desire variant

screens.prompt: Listen and complete both actions in the conditional travel plan.
scaffold: 京都に行ったら、浴衣を

after.text: 京都に行ったら、浴衣を着て、お寺を見てみたいです。
after.secondary: きょうとにいったら、ゆかたをきて、おてらをみてみたいです。

after.text: If I go to Kyoto, I would like to put on a yukata and try visiting temples.
着て is the te-form of wear; 見て is lexical see/visit. The final auxiliary みたい is kana and expresses the desired trial.

audio.text: 京都に行ったら、浴衣を着て、お寺を見てみたいです。
audio.reading: きょうとにいったら、ゆかたをきて、おてらをみてみたいです。
